title: First declension concluded; adjectives of the first and second declensions

paradigms.label: θάλαττα — First Declension (short-α)
paradigms.notes: Short α in nominative and accusative singular, but η in genitive and dative — the mixed first-declension type.

paradigms.label: νεανίᾱς — First Declension Masculine (-ᾱς)
paradigms.notes: Masculine, but first declension: the -ου genitive singular is borrowed from the second declension to mark the gender.

paradigms.label: στρατιώτης — First Declension Masculine (-ης)
paradigms.notes: Vocative in short -α with retracted accent: στρατιῶτα. Nouns in -της regularly do this.

paradigms.label: ἀγαθός — Adjective 2-1-2 (η-type), singular
paradigms.notes: Feminine in η after a consonant. Masculine and neuter share genitive and dative — the syncretism Lookup will demand you know.

paradigms.label: ἀγαθός — Adjective 2-1-2 (η-type), plural
paradigms.notes: The genitive plural is ἀγαθῶν in all three genders — one form, three cells.

paradigms.label: ἀγαθός — Adjective 2-1-2 (η-type), dual
paradigms.notes: The feminine dual ἀγαθά is spelled like the neuter plural — context alone decides.

paradigms.label: ἄξιος — Adjective 2-1-2 (ᾱ-type), singular
paradigms.notes: Feminine in ᾱ after ε, ι, ρ. The accent sits on the penult and moves nowhere it need not.

paradigms.label: ἄξιος — Adjective 2-1-2 (ᾱ-type), plural
paradigms.notes: The feminine genitive plural is ἀξίων, following the masculine's accent — NOT the noun-style perispomenon -ῶν. This is the classic adjective trap.

paradigms.label: ἄξιος — Adjective 2-1-2 (ᾱ-type), dual
paradigms.notes: The feminine dual ἀξίᾱ is spelled like the feminine nominative singular — context alone decides.
